body: Monte Titano, at 739m tall, is a dominant feature visible from almost anywhere in San Marino. For a positive identification, look for its distinctive three towers.
San Marino's landscape is characterized by smooth, agricultural hills with many small, winding roads. The vegetation is distinctly Mediterranean and typically appears lush.
San Marino's licence plates are distinctively short and white with blue lettering. This contrasts with the longer plates, often with blue strips, found in other European countries.
Road signs and bollards are generally identical to those in Italy. Many signs will give directions to the nearby Italian city of Rimini.
Similar to Italy, most utility poles in San Marino are round and made of concrete. Wooden poles can also be found.
San Marino is unique for its use of yellow chevrons with burgundy red arrows.
San Marino has unique and elaborate pedestrian crossings, which feature painted blue crosswalks and hanging signs.
Lime-green trash bins are very common in San Marino. However, in Generation 4 coverage, some have been replaced with black bins.
The Superstrada di San Marino is the only divided road in the country. It runs from Dogana to the City of San Marino and its lanes are separated by a metal guardrail.
The historic centre of San Marino is covered by a Generation 3 trekker camera.
